name: Kenney blue button • Normal
rights_note: The original Kenney UI Pack grant in this mirror expressly covers the art. The identical SVG is used by the cited Godot theme. A separate focus indicator is needed.
summary: The blue Primary Default button uses this SVG for normal. Its 64 by 64 raster sibling and matching vector are available. The upstream Godot skin uses left, top, right and bottom slices of 16, 8, 16, 12 pixels.
adaptation: Combine the five matched sprites in a single responsive button, preserve the edge widths and keep the text separate. Test a larger localized label and draw a visible keyboard focus ring.

name: Kenney RPG parchment button • Normal
rights_note: The RPG expansion license explicitly permits personal and commercial use of these graphics under CC0. The selected sprite contains no label.
summary: A 190 by 49 RGBA standalone sprite supplies the beige long command button in its normal state. Both state pictures share a width and have different heights.
adaptation: Bottom-align both states in one fixed-size hit target so the 4-pixel height difference moves the apparent surface without moving a neighboring button. Add separate hover and focus indicators for keyboard operation.

name: raygui Light button surfaces
rights_note: The raygui source explicitly grants the zlib license. This entry covers the built-in appearance constants and geometry. The overview uses its own installed display typeface.
summary: The default style defines distinct border, fill and text colors for normal, focused, pressed and disabled states. The button overrides the default border width to two pixels.
adaptation: Use the four matched color triples with their original area and border roles. Test text contrast at the target UI size and add a noncolor cue for focus.

name: Godot five-state nine-slice mapping
rights_note: The upstream README grants MIT to code and separates the third-party Kenney art. Its asset-specific CC0 text is pinned for each artwork item.
summary: BUTTON_VARIANTS and define_buttons assign normal, hover, pressed, hover-plus-pressed and disabled files and set different stretch margins for raised and flat faces. Focus uses an empty style.
adaptation: Reuse the visual state mapping and add an independent focus-ring style that survives mouse hover or press. Bind accessible disabled semantics separately from sprite choice.
